title: Question about the darker/not darker shadows at the end of Perfect Days (2023)

commenti.body:
Interesting thought. I really hadn’t interpreted the overlapping shadows as a metaphor, I just thought that it was a nice moment of connection between two strangers.

I don’t think it needs to be interpreted as a metaphor in order to enjoy or take anything from  the film, but if it is, then this is my interpretation:

The fact that the shadows don’t compound and get darker means that two people can share in the same experience, together, but also separately. This is both a nice thing and a difficult thing - that you can experience connection through being in the same space, but also in the end you are responsible and carry your own shadow, it still exists when you are on your own.

To me this is in harmony with the stoic character of the main character, who I think has learned to disregard (most) external sources of distress and can focus on how he feels at any given time. Eg: He can’t control how people look down on him as a toilet cleaner, that is external to him, but he can control how he feels about what he does, which manifests in how he does his job. The shadow you carry around is similar to your constant need to understand and live with your emotions.
